task:
BUILD PART 2 OF 3 OF F2D PR1: the ranking and API layer over the wide archetype row. Update only the existing branch codex/run-38398470499-1; its head must be a3a9d6f3d0e2d092cce110134928ce40382d16dd -- if it is not, stop and report the SHA you found. Part 1 (already on this branch) rewrote migration 011 to one wide row per system, moved the canonical model to shared_contracts/v3_system_archetype_model.py with score_raw_system and archetype_model_sha256, and recut the manifest/authority. Read part 1's diff first (git diff main...HEAD) so you build on what is actually there.

AUTHORITY: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-10-v3-finder-f2d-wide-archetype-and-product-attachment-design.md. Read CLAUDE.md first, then design sections 3.1-3.3 (the columns and indexes you query), 6 (Ranking SQL and F3 behaviour -- this part implements ALL of it), 8.7 (the anchored nearest-first rewrite and the plan assertions), and the PR1 bullet in section 10. Where this task and the design differ, the design wins. Where the design and the current code differ, follow the design and name the conflict in your summary. Do not reopen design decisions.

SCOPE. This part makes the Finder API read the wide row and bounds every ranking query. Part 3 (a later task on this branch) does scripts/v3_archetype_calibration_probe.py, scripts/dev/measure_wide_archetype_footprint.py, the two seed scripts and their tests -- DO NOT TOUCH those, and do not touch sql/, scripts/v3_system_archetype*.py or shared_contracts/ except to import from them. Their tests and the Review Lab / Cypress lanes may still fail at this head; do not edit, skip, xfail or delete them. No pull request will be opened until part 3 has landed.

ALLOWED FILES: apps/api/src/ranking/profile.py; apps/api/src/ranking/ranking_sql.py; apps/api/src/routers/archetypes.py (the /rankings path and the shared identity helper only -- /rerank, /system/{id64}, /simulate and /profiles stay legacy and untouched); apps/api/src/models.py; apps/api/src/local_search.py; the regenerated clients apps/web/src/lib/api/generated/types.gen.ts, apps/web/src/lib/api/generated/sdk.gen.ts and packages/api-client/src/generated/api.gen.ts; tests/test_ranking_profile_identity.py, tests/test_ranking_sql.py, tests/test_archetype_rankings_v3.py, tests/test_local_search_v3.py, tests/test_ranking_identity_and_no_legacy.py; tests/integration/conftest.py and tests/ratings_v4_pg_fixture.py only if the fixture must seed wide rows for these tests; CHANGES.md. Any other changed path must be justified in your summary as required by a specific failing contract test, otherwise it is a failure.

RANKING PROFILE (design section 6, first paragraphs). (a) RANKING_VERSION = 'v3-colony-potential-2'; recompute and pin ranking_sha256 through the existing drift-guard test. (b) Everything that decides a ranking enters the hashed PROFILE_SPEC via _canonical_base(): the key-to-column map archetype_columns {key: {score, tier, confidence, weighted_key}} with the confidence expression written out (ppm / 1000000.0); the floor default 60 and the accepted floor set {60, 76, 88}; the stored-key integer expression verbatim ((<key>_score::bigint * <key>_confidence_ppm * completeness_ppm) + 50000000) / 100000000; the 10,000 window and the combined offset+limit bound; the is_truncated and total = min(qualifying, 10000) rules; the hard-filter rejection set; tie_break = ["system_id64"] (was ["distance", "system_id64"]). (c) ranking_sql.py derives ARCHETYPE_COLUMNS from the spec; the route's Query(...) declarations are built from the spec's constants. (d) The identity test mutates each of these in turn and asserts the digest changes.

PICKED-ARCHETYPE QUERY: four stages, the relation touched twice (section 6). (1) Window, index-only: over v3_app.system_archetype alone, select system_id64 and <key>_weighted_e4 for the generation with the floor as a SERVER-CHOSEN LITERAL (<key>_score >= 60, >= 76 or >= 88 from a fixed three-entry map keyed by the validated min_score -- never a parameter beside it), ORDER BY <key>_weighted_e4 DESC, system_id64 ASC; the page query LIMIT 10000, the count query LIMIT 10001. (2) Join v3_app.system_search for response columns only, no filtering. (3) Page: restate ORDER BY <key>_weighted_e4 DESC, system_id64 ASC on the <= 10,000 survivors, then OFFSET/LIMIT. (4) Fetch: join v3_app.system_archetype again by primary key for the <= page_size paged rows to read the selected score, tier, confidence and the summary columns, and REPEAT the ORDER BY on the outermost SELECT. The count query uses stages 1-2 only: SELECT count(*) FROM (SELECT 1 ... LIMIT 10001) t; total = min(count, 10000); is_truncated = (count = 10001). The no-pick path keeps the v3_app.system_archetype_summary join and weighted_potential DESC NULLS LAST, system_id64 order. No user string is ever formatted into SQL as an identifier; the router rejects a key outside ARCHETYPE_KEYS with 422 before any SQL is built.

CONTRACT CHANGES, all hashed (section 6, "Contract changes in PR1"). (a) /api/archetypes/rankings: min_score: Literal[60, 76, 88] = Query(60); offset Query(0, ge=0, le=9999); limit keeps ge=1, le=500; route-level offset + limit <= 10000 else 422. (b) A picked request carrying galaxy_region, max_distance_ly, has_elw, min_slots or max_contamination is a 422 naming the parameters with the reason text "archetype ranking is unfiltered in the initial product; filter in Any mode or drop the filter". (c) Local search (apps/api/src/local_search.py): every count becomes LIMIT cap + 1 with total = min(count, cap) and total_is_capped = (count > cap) -- anchored included (today the flag is set at total >= cap, local_search.py around lines 922 and 965-970); the request model enforces from >= 0, size >= 1, from + size <= 10_000. (d) Galaxy-wide Any-mode requests carrying ANY hard filter are a 422 with reason "pick an anchor area or remove the filter". (e) Anchored Any requests keep every filter; the request's own max_distance_ly is NOT a hard filter for this classification (it is the KNN path's intrinsic radius; _v3_hard_filters records it for every anchored request, local_search.py around lines 737-743), while min_distance_ly and every other entry are. An UNFILTERED NEAREST-FIRST anchored request (sort_by='distance', no hard filter other than max_distance_ly) is accepted at any radius the route allows (default 500 ly, cap MAX_SEARCH_RADIUS 10,000 ly). Every other anchored request -- one carrying a hard filter, or one sorted by score (sort_by='development', the request default, which the route maps to score order even with an anchor) -- is capped at 500 ly and answers 422 above it with reason "reduce the radius, sort by distance, or remove the filter". (f) Additive response fields: is_truncated: bool on ArchetypeRankingsResponse (models.py has extra='forbid'); and archetype_version, archetype_manifest_sha256 and archetype_model_sha256 on the shared ranking identity of BOTH the rankings and the local-search envelopes, read from the published product row by _current_derived_generation(), which fails closed with 503 when the system_archetype product row is missing or not READY -- never an envelope without identity. (The product must be READY; the published_at requirement arrives with migration 015 in PR2, not here.)

ANCHORED NEAREST-FIRST REWRITE (section 8.7): the anchored page and its sentinel count are built around a GiST KNN scan on system_search_position_gist, limit inside and radius outside: an inner SELECT over v3_app.system_search joined to the archetype summary by primary key, WHERE position_ly <@ :bounding_cube (the index condition), ORDER BY position_ly <-> :anchor, weighted_potential DESC NULLS LAST, system_id64, LIMIT :inner_limit (offset + page, or 10,001 for the count); the outer query filters nearest.distance_ly <= :radius. Keep the existing tie-break (weighted potential, then system_id64) served by an incremental sort within each equal-distance group.

RETAINED NO-LEGACY RULES: no mv_archetype_rankings, system_archetype_scores, system_archetype_traits, FROM systems or public. in the repointed paths (tests/test_ranking_identity_and_no_legacy.py keeps asserting it). Parameterized SQL only; the floor literal is chosen from a fixed map, never from user input.

CLIENTS: regenerate all three typed clients (cd apps/web && pnpm generate:api regenerates apps/web/src/lib/api/generated/types.gen.ts, sdk.gen.ts and packages/api-client/src/generated/api.gen.ts; CI's OpenAPI drift check fails on any of them). If the runner lacks pnpm/Node or cannot start the API to capture openapi.json, say so explicitly in your summary and list the schema changes the regeneration must pick up; do not hand-edit generated files.

TESTS (section 6 "Tests" paragraph; runners have no PostgreSQL -- write the database-backed tests against the existing disposable-PG18 fixtures, seeding wide rows by inserting through the part-1 builder or direct wide-row inserts under a BUILDING product; run everything that runs without a database and list the database tests you wrote but could not run). Required: (1) identity: digest changes for each hashed element; sha pinned; tie_break is ["system_id64"]. (2) SQL builder, no DB: every key maps to its four columns and the map is derived from the spec; 60/76/88 produce the matching literal and nothing else produces SQL; the picked page SQL contains the window with LIMIT 10000, the restated ORDER BY after the join and again on the outermost SELECT; the count SQL has LIMIT 10001 and no ORDER BY; no literal user value appears in any SQL; adversarial key strings never reach SQL; the no-pick SQL keeps weighted_potential DESC NULLS LAST, system_id64; the anchored SQL has the KNN ORDER BY inside the LIMIT and the radius outside. (3) Route contracts (DB fixture): 60/76/88 accepted, 59/70/100 -> 422; offset=9999,limit=1 -> 200, offset=9999,limit=2 and offset=10000 -> 422; from=9950,size=50 ok, from=10000,size=1 and from=10001 -> 422; counts at exactly 10,000 (flag false) and 10,001 (flag true) for picked, galaxy-wide and anchored; the 422 for each hard filter on a picked request and on a galaxy-wide Any request; the same filters accepted when anchored at 500 ly; a filtered anchored request at 501 ly -> 422; a score-sorted anchored request at 501 ly -> 422; an unfiltered nearest-first anchored request at 10,000 ly accepted; a nearest-first request with min_distance_ly at 501 ly -> 422; both envelopes carry all three identity fields; a missing or non-READY archetype product -> 503 on both routes; unknown key -> 422. (4) Ordering (DB fixture): returned <key>_weighted_e4 values are non-increasing with ties by ascending system_id64 on a fixture seeded with ties, and two adjacent pages concatenate with no repeat or gap. (5) Plan tests (DB fixture, plan_cache_mode = force_generic_plan, EXPLAIN (FORMAT JSON)): for each floor the matching partial index is used, the window node is an Index Only Scan with <= 10,001 rows, the sort node's input <= 10,000, the fetch node's rows <= page_size at 50 and 500; the anchored nearest-first plan shows the KNN index scan under the inner Limit and an Incremental Sort rather than a Sort.

VALIDATION TO RUN AND REPORT WITH EXACT COUNTS: ruff check apps/api/src tests; python -m pytest tests/test_ranking_profile_identity.py tests/test_ranking_sql.py -q; every other test module you touched that runs without a database; if the API can be started locally, pnpm generate:api and git status of the generated files. Do not deploy, contact production, or use production credentials.

IF YOU CANNOT FINISH EVERYTHING IN THIS SESSION, complete in this order and stop cleanly: profile spec + ranking_sql builders, the /rankings route contract, local_search bounds and 422 rules, the anchored KNN rewrite, identity fields and 503, client regeneration, tests. State precisely what remains so the follow-up task can complete it. End with: files changed; tests run with counts; database tests written but not run; whether the clients were regenerated; and any design-versus-code conflict you found.
